title: Loops show their key, and four fixes
thisBuild: Loops show their tempo and key. In Sounds and on the Sample sheet a loop reads like "4 beats at 120 bpm · C# major / A# minor". The two names mean the same notes. 38 of the 90 Qbldy loops have a key; the others were not clear enough to name.
Search finds loops by key: type "d minor" in Sounds.

Sounds you make keep their tempo and key too. A resampled loop remembers its tempo and length, and now follows the mess's tempo like a Qbldy loop. A mic take remembers the tempo it was made at. Sounds already in Your Workbench get their key measured once, in the background.

Holding a pad no longer opens its menu by accident. Lift between about half a second and a bit over a second for the menu; hold longer and you are just playing. Pads that sound while held (synths, Sustain, gate) never open it from a hold: tap the pad, then Menu by the bank numbers.
The Tempo slider changes the tempo as it moves.
The Repeat menu in the dock is one small panel: Every, Plays, Each repeat.
The Sample button by the bank numbers now always opens the pad you tapped last. It could open the one before.
watch: Check a few loop keys by ear: set the mess to the key a loop shows and play keys over it. Send a note for any that sound wrong.
Resample a loop, change the tempo, play the resample: it should stay in time with the beat.
Hold a Sustain pad or a synth pad for a second or two and lift: no menu. Hold a drum pad for under a second and lift: menu.
Drag the Tempo slider while a loop plays: the beat should follow your finger.
limits: Keys are measured, not heard. A loop with no clear key shows none.
A resample made before this build has no tempo stored, so it does not follow the tempo.
An old Workbench sound shows its new key the next time the list is drawn.
